papers.name: The Duluth Daily Lantern
papers.character: Big-city yellow journalism; the biggest Fame multiplier.

local.headline: ORE TONNAGE BREAKS ALL RECORDS
local.deck: Zenith City Docks Load More Iron in a Week Than Any Port on Earth
local.body: The ore docks at Duluth have shipped more iron this week than in any week of their history, and the mine owners on the Mesabi say the best is yet to come. Every berth was full on Tuesday and a dozen steamers lay at anchor off the canal waiting their turn.

local.headline: McKINLEY MEN CONFIDENT
local.deck: Republicans of St. Louis County Say Prosperity Will Carry the State in November
local.body: At a rousing meeting in the Lyceum on Saturday evening the friends of the President declared that the full dinner pail would carry Minnesota again. The Bryan men, meeting across the street, said nothing of the kind.

local.headline: NEW ELEVATOR TO RISE ON RICE'S POINT
local.deck: Two Million Bushels Under One Roof; Work Begins in the Spring
local.body: The Consolidated company has let the contract for a grain elevator on Rice's Point to hold two million bushels. With it, say the board of trade, Duluth will pass Chicago for wheat before the century is out.

ads: DR. MORSE'S INDIAN ROOT PILLS cure all ills of the liver. At every druggist.
THE SPALDING HOUSE: steam heat, electric light, fifty rooms facing the lake. $2 a day.
WANTED: deckhands and firemen for the Anchor Line steamers. Apply at the canal office.

papers.name: The Superior Courier-Ledger
papers.character: Rival to Duluth; loves to blame Minnesota.

local.headline: SUPERIOR'S HARBOR THE FINER, SAYS ENGINEER
local.deck: Government Man Finds More Water at the Entry Than at the Duluth Canal
local.body: An engineer of the War Department, sounding both harbors for the river and harbor bill, reports more water at the Superior entry than at the much-boasted canal across the bay. Our friends in Minnesota are invited to read his figures.

local.headline: WHALEBACK YARD BUSY
local.deck: Two New Steel Barges on the Ways at West Superior
local.body: The shipyard at West Superior has two of Captain McDougall's steel barges on the ways and will launch the first before the month is out. Three hundred men are at work.

local.headline: MINNESOTA TAKES THE CREDIT AGAIN
local.deck: Duluth Paper Claims Wisconsin Grain as Its Own
local.body: The Duluth papers have once more reported the grain shipped from Superior's elevators as Duluth's own. This paper will go on printing the true figures, whatever is said across the bay.

ads: BADGER STATE BREWING CO. Lager on draught at every respectable house in the city.
LOTS FOR SALE in West Superior: the coming city of the Northwest. Easy terms.
Tower Avenue Hardware: stoves, lamps and ship chandlery at Duluth prices less ten per cent.

papers.name: The Ashland Ore & Lumber Gazette

local.headline: ORE DOCK LOADS RECORD SHIPMENT
local.deck: Gogebic Iron Goes Out by the Shipload; Steamers Wait in the Bay
local.body: The Soo Line dock loaded seven steamers in one day this week, a figure never seen at Ashland before. The mines of the Gogebic range report more men at work than at any time since the panic.

local.headline: SAWMILLS RUN NIGHT AND DAY
local.deck: Lumber Piles Grow Along the Shore; Prices Hold Firm
local.body: Every mill on the bay front is running a night shift, and the lumber yards stretch half a mile along the shore. Buyers from Chicago say they will take all the pine Ashland can cut.

local.headline: BROWNSTONE IN DEMAND
local.deck: Chicago Builders Order From the Bay Quarries
local.body: The quarries about the bay have orders enough for the season from builders in Chicago and Milwaukee. The stone goes south by schooner as fast as it can be cut.

ads: HOTEL CHEQUAMEGON: the finest resort hotel on the Great Lakes. Rates on application.
ASHLAND IRON & STEEL: castings, boiler work and ship repairs. Second Street.
Notice to mariners: the Ashland breakwater light is now shown from sunset.

papers.name: The Bayfield Fishermen's Weekly
papers.character: Local gossip, fish and the weather.

local.headline: HERRING RUNS HEAVY OFF SAND ISLAND
local.deck: Tugs Come In Down to Their Rails; Packers Short of Barrels
local.body: The herring have come in thick off Sand Island and the north end of Madeline, and every tug in the fleet came in loaded this week. The packing houses are short of barrels and the cooper has taken on two hands.

local.headline: BROWNSTONE QUARRY HIRES FIFTY
local.body: The quarry on Basswood Island has taken on fifty men for the season and expects to ship stone to Chicago until the ice. Board is found on the island.

local.headline: STRAWBERRY SOCIAL A SUCCESS
local.deck: Ladies of the Methodist Church Raise Twelve Dollars
local.body: The strawberry social at the Methodist church on Thursday evening was well attended, and the ladies raised twelve dollars toward the new bell. Several of the fishing captains were present, by special request of their wives.

ads: BOUTIN & MAHAN: fresh and salt fish, nets and twine. City dock.
Island View Hotel: clean beds, good meals, 50 cents. Near the dock.
LOST: a gill net, 40 boxes, off Oak Island. Reward for its return. Inquire at this office.

plain.headline: A FALSE LIGHT IN {REGION}
plain.deck: {Victim} Lured Onto a Shoal; {WHO} Named
plain.body: {Victim} went onto a shoal in {region} by night, her master steering for what he took to be the lighthouse. Witnesses say the light was a lantern on a pole, and that {who} hung it there. {Dead} drowned.

lurid.headline: THE MOON-CUSSER!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Hangs a Lantern on the Rocks and Lures {Victim} to Her Doom
lurid.body: Wreckers' work in {region}, and {epithet} {who} behind it. A false light on the point, a ship steering for it, and {dead} drowned in the dark while the wreckers waited with their boats. The lake has not seen such villainy.

unnamed.headline: A FALSE LIGHT IN {REGION}?
unnamed.deck: {Victim} Ashore; Her Crew Swear They Steered for a Light
unnamed.body: {Victim} went onto a shoal in {region} by night. Her people say they had a light fair on the bow where the lighthouse should be, and the keeper swears his own was burning true. Old hands say 'moon-cussers', and the revenue men are asking who. {Dead} drowned.

plain.headline: SMUGGLING IN THE ISLANDS
plain.deck: {WHO} Seen Trading With the Island Smuggler by Night
plain.body: {who} was seen alongside the smuggler's boat in the islands after dark, and the matter has been reported to the authorities in {region}. The revenue men say they have their eye on the islands.

lurid.headline: {WHO} AT IT AGAIN!
lurid.deck: Midnight Rendezvous With the Whiskey Smugglers; Revenue Men Helpless
lurid.body: Once more {epithet} {who} has been seen consorting with the island smugglers under cover of darkness. Honest men in {region} ask how long the government means to let it go on.

unnamed.headline: LIGHTS IN THE ISLANDS
unnamed.deck: A Schooner Seen Alongside the Smuggler's Boat
unnamed.body: {who} was seen alongside a boat known to the revenue men in the islands after dark. Who she was, nobody could say.

plain.headline: UNTAXED WHISKEY FOUND
plain.deck: {WHO} Caught With Smuggled Liquor at {port}
plain.body: A merchant at {port} found the goods offered by {who} were smuggled, and sent for the revenue man. The matter is before the authorities in {region}.

lurid.headline: RUM RUNNER {WHO}!
lurid.deck: Barrels of Smuggled Spirits Offered Brazenly at {port}
lurid.body: {epithet} {who} had the gall to offer smuggled whiskey to an honest merchant at {port}, in broad daylight. The revenue service is said to be furious.

plain.headline: STOLEN GOODS OFFERED
plain.deck: {WHO} Tried to Sell Marked Cargo at {port}
plain.body: A merchant at {port} knew the marks on goods offered him by {who} as stolen, and told the constable. The owners have been informed.

lurid.headline: FENCING PIRATE'S LOOT!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Hawks Stolen Cargo on the {port} Waterfront
lurid.body: {epithet} {who} walked into a store at {port} with stolen goods and asked a fair price for them. The merchant knew the marks. Where will it end?

plain.headline: CARGO STOLEN BY ITS CARRIER
plain.deck: {WHO} Sold a Shipper's Goods and Kept the Money
plain.body: Freight entrusted to {who} at {port} never reached its consignee: the cargo was sold off on the way. The shipper's agents up and down the lake have been warned.

lurid.headline: BRAZEN THEFT ON THE LAKE
lurid.deck: {WHO} Robs the Shippers Who Trusted the Vessel
lurid.body: {epithet} {who} took a cargo in good faith at {port}, as the shippers believed, and sold every barrel of it. No shipper on the lake will trust that vessel again, and the law in {region} is looking.

plain.headline: FIRED ON OFF {REGION}
plain.deck: {WHO} Put a Shot Across the Bows of {Victim}
plain.body: The master of {victim}, of {owner}, reports that {who} fired on his vessel in {region} without warning or cause. The matter has been laid before the authorities.

lurid.headline: GUNFIRE ON THE LAKE!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Opens Fire on {Victim}
lurid.body: Peaceable shipping is no longer safe in {region}. {Epithet} {who} fired upon {victim} in open water, and her crew made port shaken. How long will the government sit on its hands?

unnamed.headline: SHOTS FIRED IN {REGION}
unnamed.body: The crew of {victim} report a gun fired across their bows in {region} by {who}. They could not make out the vessel.

plain.headline: PIRACY IN {REGION}
plain.deck: {Victim} Stopped and Robbed by {WHO}
plain.body: {Victim}, of {owner}, was brought to under the guns of {who} in {region} and robbed of {taken}. Her crew gave the authorities a full description when they made port. Dead: {dead}.

lurid.headline: PIRATES ON LAKE SUPERIOR!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Plunders {Victim}; {Owner} Demands Action
lurid.body: In a deed not seen on these waters in living memory, {epithet} {who} ran down {victim} in {region}, held her crew at the muzzle of a gun and carried off {taken}. {Dead} died in the affair. {Owner} has offered every assistance to the law.

unnamed.headline: ROBBERY ON THE OPEN LAKE
unnamed.body: The crew of {victim}, of {owner}, report being stopped in {region} by {who} and robbed of {taken}. Of the robbers' vessel they could tell little.

plain.headline: {VICTIM} SENT TO THE BOTTOM
plain.deck: Sunk in {Region}; {WHO} Named
plain.body: {Victim}, of {owner}, went to the bottom in {region}, and {who} is named as the cause of it. Dead: {dead}. Shipping men all round the lake are in an uproar, and the underwriters are said to be offering a reward.

lurid.headline: SCUTTLED!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Sinks {Victim} in Cold Blood
lurid.body: {epithet} {who} has sent {victim} to the bottom of {region}. {Dead} lost. {Owner} is beside itself, and every master on the lake now sails with one eye over his shoulder.

unnamed.headline: VESSEL LOST IN {REGION}
unnamed.deck: Foul Play Feared in the Loss of {Victim}
unnamed.body: {Victim}, of {owner}, has gone down in {region}. Survivors speak of {who} alongside her before she sank. Dead: {dead}.

plain.headline: MURDER ON THE LAKE
plain.deck: {Dead} Killed Aboard {Victim}; {WHO} Wanted
plain.body: {Dead} of the crew of {victim}, of {owner}, lost their lives at the hands of {who} in {region}. The authorities have sworn out a warrant, and the families are in mourning.

lurid.headline: BLOODY WORK IN {REGION}!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Leaves {Dead} Dead Aboard {Victim}
lurid.body: The lake runs red. {Epithet} {who} has murdered {dead} of the crew of {victim} in {region}. Ministers preached on it Sunday, and a public meeting demands the government do its duty.

unnamed.headline: DEATH IN {REGION}
unnamed.body: {Dead} of the crew of {victim} met their deaths in {region} at the hands of {who}. Who the killers were is not known.

plain.headline: REVENUE CUTTER FIRED ON
plain.deck: {WHO} Turns a Gun on the Morrill in {Region}
plain.body: The revenue cutter Morrill was fired upon in {region} by {who}. Her commander has orders to take the vessel by any means, and the government has declared the captain an outlaw.

lurid.headline: WAR ON THE GOVERNMENT!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Fires on the Morrill; Outlaw Declared
lurid.body: {epithet} {who} has fired on a vessel of the United States in {region}. There is no word for it but rebellion. The Morrill's guns are run out, and the captain will hang.

plain.headline: REVENUE MEN SEIZE CARGO
plain.deck: {goods} Taken From {WHO}
plain.body: Officers of the revenue service searched {who} in {region} and seized {goods}. The vessel was allowed to proceed.

lurid.headline: {goods} SEIZED!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Caught Red-Handed by the Revenue Men
lurid.body: The revenue officers who boarded {epithet} {who} in {region} found {goods} hidden in the hold, by their own count. More, they suspect, went over the side.

plain.headline: THE LAW HUNTS {WHO}
plain.deck: Authorities in {region} Want the Vessel Stopped
plain.body: The authorities in {region} have put out word that {who} is to be stopped and searched wherever found. The revenue cutter has been told.

lurid.headline: {WHO} HUNTED!
lurid.deck: {region} Up in Arms; {reward}
lurid.body: {epithet} {who} is wanted by every officer in {region}, and the revenue cutter has steam up to find the vessel. The waterfront talks of nothing else.

plain.headline: WANTED: DEAD OR ALIVE
plain.deck: {WHO}; {reward}
plain.body: The authorities in {region} have declared {who} an outlaw. Any officer may take the captain, dead or alive, and capture means the rope. Citizens with knowledge of the vessel are asked to come forward.

plain.headline: TAKEN BY THE MORRILL
plain.deck: {WHO} Brought Into {port} Under Guard
plain.body: The revenue cutter Morrill took {who} on the lake in {region}. The captain is held at {port}, and the vessel impounded.

lurid.headline: {WHO} IN IRONS!
lurid.deck: The Cutter Gets Its Prey at Last; Crowds at the Dock
lurid.body: After a chase the waterfront will talk of for years, the revenue cutter Morrill brought {epithet} {who} into {port} in irons. A crowd gathered at the dock to see the captain marched to the lockup.

plain.headline: OUT OF THE LOCKUP
plain.deck: {WHO} Free Again at {port}
plain.body: {who} walked out of the {port} lockup this week, and the vessel has been released from impound.

plain.headline: CUTTER OUTRUN
plain.deck: {WHO} Gets Clear of the Morrill in {region}
plain.body: The revenue cutter Morrill gave chase to {who} in {region}, but lost the vessel. The cutter's officers decline to say how.

lurid.headline: {WHO} LAUGHS AT THE LAW!
lurid.deck: The Morrill Left Wallowing as the Pirate Shows a Clean Pair of Heels
lurid.body: With every gun on the revenue cutter Morrill trained on the vessel, {epithet} {who} put up the helm and was gone. Old hands on the {town} waterfront say there's no schooner on the lake could do it, and yet it was done.

unnamed.headline: CUTTER GIVES UP THE CHASE
unnamed.deck: A Schooner Outruns the Morrill in {region}
unnamed.body: The revenue cutter Morrill gave chase to {who} in {region} and lost her. Her name is not known.

plain.headline: FINED AT {PORT}
plain.deck: {WHO} Settles With the Harbor Master
plain.body: {who} paid a fine to the harbor master at {port} this week for breaches of the harbor rules in {region}.

plain.headline: A SMART PASSAGE
plain.deck: {WHO} Delivers in Record Time
plain.body: {who} brought a cargo into {port} in better time than the shippers had any right to expect. It is the kind of seamanship that keeps the lake trade honest.

lurid.headline: FASTEST SCHOONER ON THE LAKE?
lurid.deck: {WHO} Shatters the Record Into {port}
lurid.body: Old masters on the {town} waterfront shook their heads at the time {epithet} {who} made into {port}. The shippers are said to be lining up.

plain.headline: FIRST BOAT IN!
plain.deck: {WHO} Opens the Season at {port}
plain.body: The first vessel of the season to make {port} after the ice was {who}. The whole town turned out to the dock to see her in, and the captain was given the customary silk hat.

plain.headline: ASHORE IN THE NIGHT
plain.deck: {Victim} on a Shoal in {region}
plain.body: {Victim} went onto a shoal in {region} in the night, in thick weather. Her master says he had the light where it should be. {Dead} drowned. The underwriters have sent a man.

plain.headline: ANOTHER WRECK IN {REGION}
plain.deck: {Victim} Lost; The Lake Takes Its Toll
plain.body: {Victim} struck in {region} after dark and lies there now. {Dead} drowned. Masters say the islands are a bad place in a blow, lights or no lights.

plain.headline: WRECKS UNDER INQUIRY
plain.deck: Too Many Ships Lost Near One Light in {region}; the Revenue Service Sends the Morrill
plain.body: After a run of strandings near the same light in {region}, the Lighthouse Service and the revenue men have opened an inquiry. The cutter Morrill has been ordered to the islands. Old hands whisper of moon-cussers; the keeper swears his light burned true.

plain.headline: IN THROUGH THE GALE
plain.deck: {WHO} Makes {port} With the Storm Signal Flying
plain.body: With the storm signal up and the sea breaking white across the entrance, {who} came into {port} under shortened sail and made fast without a scratch. Watchers on the dock gave a cheer.

plain.headline: WHO IS {NICK}?
plain.deck: The Waterfront's Name for Captain {captain} of the Schooner {ship}
plain.body: Along the docks of {region} there is a name passed from mouth to mouth, and this paper has run it to earth: it belongs to Captain {captain}, master of the schooner {ship}. Ask a longshoreman who {nick} is and he will lower his voice. Ask the harbor master and he will tell you to mind your own business.

plain.headline: {NICK}!
plain.deck: Captain {captain} of the {ship} Has Earned a Name on the Lake
plain.body: The fishermen of {region} have had a name for the master of the schooner {ship} for some weeks, and from this issue so does the {town} paper: {nick}. Captain {captain} is not thought to care for it. The lake does not ask.

lurid.headline: THE LAKE KNOWS {NICK}
lurid.deck: Captain {captain} Earns a Name No Honest Master Would Want
lurid.body: Mothers in {region} hush their children with it and the insurance men say it under their breath: {nick}. The bearer of that name is Captain {captain} of the schooner {ship}, and this paper prints it so that every master on the lake may know whom to watch for.

plain.headline: {OLDNICK} NO MORE
plain.deck: The Waterfront Has a New Name for Captain {captain}: {Nick}
plain.body: Those who called Captain {captain} of the schooner {ship} {oldnick} are calling the captain something else this week. The new name, heard first in {region}, is {nick}, and by the look of things it will stick.

plain.headline: A NEW NAME ON THE LAKE
plain.deck: {Oldnick} Is Now {Nick}, the Docks Say
plain.body: The saloons of {region} have tired of the old name for the master of the schooner {ship}. Captain {captain}, lately {oldnick}, goes by {nick} along the waterfront now, whether the captain likes it or not.

plain.headline: MOON-CUSSERS IN THE ISLANDS
plain.deck: Wreckers Said to Be at Work Among the Apostles
plain.body: Talk on the {town} waterfront has it that {who} has learned the old wreckers' trade: a lantern on the point on a black night, and a ship steering for it onto the rocks.

lurid.headline: {WHO}, MOON-CUSSER!
lurid.deck: The Pirate Turns Wrecker; No Light on the Lake Can Be Trusted
lurid.body: {Epithet} {who}, not content with robbing ships, now lures them to their doom with lights on the rocks. Masters in {region} say they no longer know which lights to trust.

plain.headline: A CAPTAIN WHO SAVES
plain.deck: {WHO} Said to Have Money Put By
plain.body: Talk on the {town} waterfront has it that {who} has a tidy sum put by somewhere among the islands. Bankers in {region} have not seen a cent of it.

plain.headline: WHERE DOES THE MONEY GO?
plain.deck: {WHO} Rumored to Be Worth Ten Thousand Dollars
plain.body: {who} is said to be worth ten thousand dollars and more, though no bank in {region} holds it. Old hands guess at a strongbox in the islands.

lurid.headline: {WHO}'S HIDDEN HOARD!
lurid.deck: Ten Thousand in Gold, the Waterfront Swears
lurid.body: Every loafer on the {town} waterfront has a theory about where {epithet} {who} keeps the money. None of them has found it, and none of them has stopped looking.

plain.headline: A FORTUNE AMONG THE ISLANDS
plain.deck: {WHO} Among the Richest Masters on the Lake
plain.body: It is said in {region} that {who} has put by a fortune of fifty thousand dollars, which would make the captain richer than half the shipowners in {town}. Where it is kept, nobody can say.

lurid.headline: PIRATE GOLD!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Sits on Fifty Thousand, Hidden Who Knows Where
lurid.body: The fortune of {epithet} {who} is the talk of the lake. Fifty thousand dollars, they say, and some say twice that, buried or banked or sunk in a strongbox among the Apostles.

plain.headline: A NAME ON EVERY LIP
plain.deck: {WHO} the Talk of {region}
plain.body: There is hardly a saloon in {region} where the name of {who} has not come up this week. The authorities say they are watching.

lurid.headline: WHO IS {WHO}?
lurid.deck: The Name Every Saloon on the Lake Is Whispering
lurid.body: They say {epithet} {who} cannot be caught, cannot be outrun, and cannot be bribed, though the last is disputed. Every saloon on the lake has a story, and every story is bigger than the last.

plain.headline: A LEGEND OF THE LAKE
plain.deck: {WHO} Spoken Of From Duluth to the Soo
plain.body: Not since the days of the timber pirates has a captain been talked of as {who} is talked of now. Mothers in {town} are said to use the name to frighten children.

lurid.headline: THE LEGEND OF {WHO}
lurid.deck: Half the Lake Believes It, the Other Half Wants To
lurid.body: Songs are sung about {epithet} {who} in the saloons of {town}, and the authorities in {region} would give a great deal to end them. The captain, so far, has given them nothing.

plain.headline: THE MORRILL OUTRUN AGAIN
plain.deck: Third Time {WHO} Has Got Clear of the Cutter
plain.body: For the third time the revenue cutter Morrill has given chase to {who} and lost the vessel. Questions are being asked of her captain in {town}.

lurid.headline: THREE TIMES!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Makes a Fool of the Revenue Service Once More
lurid.body: The Morrill has now lost {epithet} {who} three times over, and the waterfront in {town} has begun to keep score. The revenue service declines to comment.

plain.headline: STILL AT LARGE
plain.deck: {WHO} Free a Week With a Price on the Captain's Head
plain.body: A week has passed since the authorities in {region} declared {who} an outlaw, and the captain is still at large. Officers are said to be searching the islands.

lurid.headline: THE LAW HELPLESS!
lurid.deck: A Week Outlawed and {WHO} Still Walks Free
lurid.body: Seven days after {region} put a price on the head of {epithet} {who}, the captain has not been taken. {reward}, and no one has collected it.

plain.headline: AS GOOD AS THE CAPTAIN'S WORD
plain.deck: {WHO} Has Delivered Twenty-Five Cargoes on Time
plain.body: The freight agents of {region} report that {who} has now delivered twenty-five cargoes without once being late. Shippers in {town} speak well of the captain.

plain.headline: WELCOME IN EVERY PORT
plain.deck: {WHO} Counted a Friend by Merchants in Three Ports
plain.body: Merchants in three ports of the lake now count {who} among their best friends in the trade. There is talk of {town} being the next.

plain.headline: FASTEST SCHOONER ON THE LAKE
plain.deck: {WHO} Has Made Three Record Passages
plain.body: With a third cargo brought into {port} in record time, {who} has the shippers of {region} lining up. Old masters say it can't last.

plain.headline: THE GALES OF NOVEMBER
plain.deck: {WHO} Comes In Through the Worst of It
plain.body: With a November gale blowing and the storm signal up, {who} brought the vessel into {port} when steamers twice the size were running for shelter. It was a thing to see.

plain.headline: TWO LAIRS IN THE ISLANDS?
plain.deck: {WHO} Said to Keep More Than One Hideout
plain.body: Fishermen in {region} say {who} keeps not one hideout but two, one among the Apostles and one on the mainland shore. The authorities have found neither.

plain.headline: A PIRATE'S TOWN
plain.deck: {WHO} Has Built a Settlement in the Wilds, Fishermen Say
plain.body: Fishermen passing the islands report buildings where none stood a year ago: storehouses, a pier, and smoke from a chimney. They say it is the work of {who}.

lurid.headline: A PIRATE CITY!
lurid.deck: {WHO}'s Stronghold Grows by the Week
lurid.body: Where there was wilderness, {epithet} {who} has raised a stronghold of storehouses and piers. Steamer captains give the place a wide berth.

plain.headline: A SCHOONER BUILT IN THE WOODS
plain.deck: {WHO} Launches a Vessel Off a Slipway of the Captain's Own
plain.body: {who} has built and launched a schooner off a slipway in the wilds, without a shipyard or a yard bill. Shipwrights in {town} are not pleased.

plain.headline: A CARGO WON AT CARDS
plain.deck: {WHO} Takes a Vessel's Freight on a Single Hand
plain.body: It is told along the waterfront that {who} sat down to a game of draw poker and got up the owner of another captain's cargo. The loser is said to have gone back to his vessel with an empty hold.

lurid.headline: PIRATE CLEANS OUT THE CARD TABLE!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Wins a Whole Cargo, and Nobody Dares Ask How
lurid.body: {epithet} {who} is said to have won a cargo at cards in one sitting. Those who were at the table do not care to say whether the deal was straight.

plain.headline: THE ISLANDS' DEER
plain.deck: Game Wardens Hear of Venison Sold by the Hundredweight
plain.body: The camps up the shore are eating venison all winter, and none of it shot by the men eating it. Talk on the {town} waterfront names {who} as the source, and the islands' deer as the poorer for it.

lurid.headline: THE VENISON KING!
lurid.deck: {WHO} Strips the Apostles of Their Deer
lurid.body: {epithet} {who} has made a trade of slaughtering the island deer and selling the meat to the camps in open defiance of the game laws, the wardens powerless to stop it.

plain.headline: THE LUCERNE'S GOLD COMES UP
plain.deck: Strongbox Lost With the Schooner in '86 Raised Off Long Island
plain.body: The strongbox of the schooner Lucerne, lost with all hands off Long Island fourteen years ago, has been grappled up from her hull by {who}, who would not say what was in it. Old salvagers on the {town} waterfront are said to be sick with envy.

lurid.headline: {WHO} ROBS THE DROWNED!
lurid.deck: The Lucerne's Gold Taken From Her Grave
lurid.body: Not content with the living, {epithet} {who} has gone down to the Lucerne's dead for her captain's strongbox. The fishermen's lantern off Long Island, it seems, was no ghost after all.

plain.headline: THE HERMIT ISLAND PAYROLL FOUND
plain.deck: Gold Missing Since the Panic of '93 Dug Up Behind a Clerk's Cabin
plain.body: The last payroll of the Hermit Island quarry, which vanished the week the company failed, has been dug up on the island by {who}. Quarrymen in {town} who were never paid are asking where their share is.

plain.headline: NO GHOST ON MINNESOTA POINT
plain.deck: Smugglers' Cache Dug Up Below the Dead Light
plain.body: The lantern seen in the old Minnesota Point tower on moonless nights was a smuggling ring's signal, and its takings were buried at the tower's foot. They were dug up this week by {who}, says talk along the {town} waterfront.

plain.headline: THE DEVIL'S GROTTO GIVES UP ITS SECRET
plain.deck: A Drowned Smuggler's Hoard Found in the Sea Caves
plain.body: The third cave on Devils Island, where a smuggler went in one calm night and never came out, has given up his hoard to {who}, who went in at the dark of the moon as the old tale said.

plain.headline: OUTER ISLAND'S GHOST NET EXPLAINED
plain.deck: A Drowned Fisherman's Hoard Under His Fish House Floor
plain.body: The nets of Pedersen, the Outer Island fisherman lost at sea, kept coming up with brass and glass. {Who} has found why: he'd been working an old wreck alone and hid what he raised under his fish house floor.

plain.headline: A COPYCAT'S HOARD DUG UP
plain.deck: Pirate's Plunder Taken From Under a Spruce Stump
plain.body: The hoard of one of the lake's would-be pirates, beaten at sea this season, has been dug up above his camp among the islands by {who}. The papers are not sure whether to call it justice.
